subject.title: Telegram: unquarantine skipped sticker e2e tests

question: Should Telegram still require a dedicated static WEBP sticker metadata e2e case, or is the current resolver/context/cache-refresh coverage sufficient to close this issue?
rationale: Current main only partially matches the original unskip criteria, and protected live labels route the remaining coverage choice to maintainers rather than autonomous repair.

options.title: Require the static WEBP e2e
options.body: Keep this issue open and add one deterministic e2e case proving first-seen static WEBP `<media:sticker>` metadata.

options.title: Accept current coverage
options.body: Close this issue only after a Telegram owner states that existing resolver, context, and cache-refresh tests cover the risk well enough without the original e2e title.

recommendation.title: Require the static WEBP e2e
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and add one deterministic e2e case proving first-seen static WEBP `<media:sticker>` metadata.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the stabilization PR that introduced the quarantine and opened this follow-up boundary.
